For the combined N5+N4 Tanoshii book, which does not mark which of its kanji are N5 vs N4, the remaining 11 kanji were assigned N4 as an EDITORIAL DEFAULT (N5 treated as the tighter, more standardized set) -- this is NOT sourced data. notes: JLPT publishes no official kanji list for N5/N4/N3/N2 post-2010; this dataset uses a widely-used community-compiled grouping. See README for details.

170 of 2381 kanji were added from Han tu Tanoshii's own broader grouping (not present in the tanos.co.uk/jlpt_new list). Of those, 11 came from the combined N5+N4 Tanoshii book and were assigned N4 as an editorial default (that book does not distinguish N5 from N4 per character) -- see sources.hantuTanoshiiLevelGrouping. The N3, N2, and N1 Tanoshii-only extras are unambiguous (single-level source books).

19 kanji have no entry in either the CC-CEDICT or Unihan Han-Viet sources (mostly Japan-only shinjitai forms with no matching Chinese-character-set entry) and were left with hanViet: [] rather than guessed.
